title: Generic Accepted-Commit Receipt and Transaction-Safe Side-Effect Handoff

base.source_lineage: F-WOF35 composed postimage plus F-WOF36 metadata-only owner closeout

trigger.reason: The physical F-KT commit point is owned by F-MR/F-KT. A domain-specific postcommit wrapper cannot guarantee that expected side-effect admission failures occur before physical publication.

goal: Qualify a generic, domain-independent runtime seam that emits non-forgeable proof of one actual successful F-KT candidate commit, while keeping every expected failure condition before physical publication. The seam must be sufficient for domain owners to prevalidate trial-local metadata before commit and perform a total/non-recoverable-error publication after receipt issuance without moving F-KT commit authority out of the kernel transaction owner.

candidates.name: postcommit callback or observer
candidates.risk: Arbitrary domain callback code can fail after physical state publication, creating a normal-error partial composition state.

candidates.name: generic accepted commit receipt
candidates.reason: Runtime can derive immutable provenance only after did_commit=true, with no domain import or domain mutation in the physical commit path. Domain-specific expected errors can be prevalidated before commit.

candidates.name: embed all optional domain side effects inside kernel physical state
candidates.risk: Would broaden kernel state ownership and couple generic physical publication to optional process-state composition before necessity is established.

questions: Can a receipt be generated only from a successful actual F-KT commit and remain non-forgeable outside F-MR?
Can its lineage, origin revision, committed revision, t0 and t1 be source-bound without changing F-KT semantics?
Can all receipt validation that may return a normal status occur before kernel_commit_candidate?
Can the postcommit receipt materialization be total and allocation-free?
Can rejected and commit-rejected candidates produce no ready receipt?
Can receipt support remain optional with no persistent per-column allocation for inactive domains?
Can MultiSWAP ordering and A-B-A replay remain deterministic?

candidate_receipt_contract.creation_authority: F-MR commit helper only after did_commit=true
candidate_receipt_contract.time_relation: receipt t0/t1 are exactly the candidate origin interval admitted by F-KT

precommit: domain owner may separately prevalidate its attempt-local payload against checkpoint/candidate provenance
candidate_runtime_composition.commit: existing F-KT fmr_commit_candidate/kernel_commit_candidate remains authoritative and unchanged unless evidence proves a minimal API extension is required
candidate_runtime_composition.postcommit: on did_commit=true, produce receipt by total assignment from already prevalidated candidate/checkpoint metadata or authoritative committed provenance; no domain callback is invoked
candidate_runtime_composition.reject: receipt remains not-ready and domain attempt-local scratch is discarded by its owner

hard_holds: No WOFOST, snow, irrigation or other process-specific imports in the generic receipt module.
Do not weaken F-KT lineage, revision, time, mass or candidate validation.
Do not make a receipt sufficient to forge or directly mutate committed state.
Do not allocate optional domain state for inactive columns.
Do not claim crash/restart atomicity for external side effects; restart ownership remains a separate gate.
Do not change physics, numerical policy or mass accounting.
Do not move canonical integration refs in this workunit.
qualification_after_gate_A: real commit creates exactly one ready receipt
commit rejection creates no ready receipt
stale revision, lineage mismatch and time mismatch create no ready receipt
receipt provenance exactly matches checkpoint/candidate/committed transition
no postcommit normal-error branch in receipt creation
source scan proving no domain-specific dependency
